messages.subject: bug in bernoulli_logit_log
parts:
I just found a bug in the derivative of bernoulli_logit. I don't know how it passed the old tests, but after a rewrite of all the agrad tests, the bug was exposed. Anyway, it's been fixed. I just pushed the changes now. Hopefully the tests pass on Jenkins.

I'm having a little trouble with compiling in Mac under g++ at optimization level 0 (zero) with the new tests. I haven't had a chance to try other optimization levels. I think it was a bus error. I don't know what that means.


Daniel

I just found a bug in the derivative of bernoulli_logit. I don't know how it passed the old tests, but after a rewrite
of all the agrad tests, the bug was exposed. Anyway, it's been fixed. I just pushed the changes now. Hopefully the tests
pass on Jenkins.

How bad was it?  I don't see how we could've
survived HMC with a broken bernoulli_logit because

Not bad, although it's still a bug. I switched a sign in the gradient, but the gradient was guaranteed to be close to 0. As in 1e-11. I think my old tests allowed a little more tolerance, which is why it passed.

I'm having a little trouble with compiling in Mac under g++ at optimization level 0 (zero) with the new tests.

clang++ -O0 works fine. :-)
Yeah, I'm compiling with clang++ just fine.

I can't even compile with g++ as is from the makefile
because it doesn't like the -std+gnu++0x.  Where'd that
come from?
I added that to build with the changes to the tests. I forgot that we're still using g++ 4.2, which doesn't allow it. My default g++ is 4.6.

We shouldn't be using any C++11 features in building the
lib, right?

~/stan>make CC=g++ O=0 test-unit
i686-apple-darwin11-llvm-g++-4.2: src/stan/model/model_header.hpp: linker input file unused because linking not done
g++ -I src -I lib/eigen_3.1.2 -I lib/boost_1.52.0 -O0 -Wall -Wno-unused-function   -c -std=gnu++0x -I lib/gtest_1.6.0/include -I lib/gtest_1.6.0 lib/gtest_1.6.0/src/gtest-all.cc -o test/gtest.o
cc1plus: error: unrecognized command line option "-std=gnu++0x"
make: *** [test/gtest.o] Error 1
That's correct. I added that option to the google test flags, but not to the general c++ flags.

I haven't
had a chance to try other optimization levels. I think it was a bus error. I don't know what that means.

Accessing memory you shouldn't.
Argh. I'll try to track it down.
